papers.version_note: Text is the lesson page of the QCi resource library; the text layer includes site navigation and LaTeX source for the equations. One sentence in the Lorenz paragraph is garbled and one in the sum frequency paragraph reads as an error (see those assertions).
papers.what_it_is: A vendor educational web lesson from Quantum Computing Inc explaining linear versus nonlinear mathematical models and why nonlinear optics is needed for quantum optics and reservoir systems.

assertions.value: The lesson states that a mathematical model is linear when its solutions obey the property of superposition, and nonlinear when they do not.
quotes: The question of whether a mathematical model is linear essentially asks whether the solutions obey the property of superposition. Linear models obey this property and nonlinear models do not.
assertions.certainty_reason: The lesson defines linearity this way in its second section.

assertions.value: The authors state that a completely linear neural network, no matter how large, could be described by simple matrix-vector multiplication, and that even simple nonlinearity makes a neural network much more powerful.
quotes: a completely linear neural network, no matter how large, could be described by simple matrix-vector multiplication
even simple nonlinearity can make a neural network much more powerful
assertions.reader_inference: A standard textbook point; the lesson gives no proof.

assertions.value: The authors state that neural networks need some nonlinearity to be suitable for sophisticated learning tasks.
quotes: neural networks need some nonlinearity to be suitable for sophisticated learning tasks

assertions.value: The authors state that differentiation is a linear operation, so the derivative of a sum of two functions equals the sum of their derivatives, and that arbitrarily high-order derivatives also obey superposition.
quotes: so differentiation is a linear operation
Since higher-order derivatives are defined by repeatedly applying the same definition, arbitrarily high-order derivatives also obey superposition.
assertions.certainty_reason: The lesson states the property as part of its account of a linear differential equation.

assertions.value: The authors state that a differential equation involving only sums of constants, first powers of a variable, and arbitrarily high derivatives of that variable is linear, and that terms such as the square of the variable, the product of the variable with its derivative, and the square of the derivative are nonlinear.
quotes: any differential equation involving sums of constants, first powers of a variable
will be linear.
are nonlinear.
assertions.reader_inference: The three nonlinear terms are printed as LaTeX in the text layer, so the quotes hold only the connecting words.

assertions.value: The authors state that the presence of any nonlinear terms makes the entire differential equation nonlinear.
quotes: The presence of any nonlinear terms makes the entire differential equation nonlinear.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a rule of the definition.

assertions.value: The authors state that nonlinearity is a mathematical property, not a physical one, and that calling a physical system linear or nonlinear is a convenient shorthand that is not mathematically rigorous.
quotes: It is important to remember that nonlinearity is a mathematical property, not a physical one.
Such terminology, however, is not mathematically rigorous, it is just a convenient shorthand.
assertions.certainty_reason: The lesson states how it uses the terms.

assertions.value: The authors state that linear systems of differential equations tend to be much easier to solve than nonlinear systems, because new solutions can be built by summing known solutions.
quotes: Mathematically, linear systems of differential equations tend to be much easier to solve than nonlinear systems.
new solutions can be built by summing up already known solutions

assertions.value: The authors give matrix diagonalization as an example: a complete set of eigenvectors is generated and summed to solve how a system behaves from any starting point, and they state that such techniques do not work for nonlinear systems of equations.
quotes: a technique known as matrix diagonalization where a complete set of eigenvectors
Such techniques do not work for nonlinear systems of equations.

assertions.value: The authors present the Lorenz attractor as a solution to the nonlinear Lorenz equations of fluid dynamics, where superposition does not work and two very similar starting conditions diverge quickly in time.
quotes: a Lorenz attractor , which arises as a solution to a set of nonlinear differential equations known as the Lorenz equations which arise in fluid dynamics
In fact, the difference between two very similar starting conditions will grow quickly in time until their behavior is very different.

assertions.value: The authors state that linear equations can never have chaotic solutions, although nonlinear equations will not always have chaotic solutions.
quotes: chaotic linear equations can never have chaotic solutions, although nonlinear equations will not always have chaotic solutions
assertions.reader_inference: The source sentence is garbled in the text layer ('A solution with this property is known that chaotic linear equations ...'); the intended claim is the one quoted.

assertions.value: The authors state that the same system can sometimes be described in both a linear and a nonlinear way, which is not a paradox because physical models are approximations, and that the linearity of the model depends on which approximations are made.
quotes: The same system can sometimes be described in both a linear and nonlinear way.
The linearity or nonlinearity of the model depends on which approximations are made.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as the lesson's framing of what the terms apply to.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Schroedinger equation is linear in quantum amplitudes, the summing of which describes quantum interference, but that the number of states in multi-particle systems tends to grow exponentially with the number of particles, so the linear equation quickly becomes too large to solve.
quotes: is linear in quantum amplitudes, the summing of which describes quantum interference
the number of possible states described in multi-particle quantum systems tends to grow exponentially with the number of particles

assertions.value: The authors state that nonlinear optics can be described in a quantum mechanical, technically linear way, but that the practical description is often in terms of light particles rather than amplitudes, and that in nonlinear optics the light particles do not obey superposition.
quotes: While nonlinear optics can be described in a quantum mechanical (and technically linear) way
In nonlinear optics, the light particles do not obey superposition and are therefore not described in a linear way.
assertions.reader_inference: Read strictly, a linear quantum theory still obeys superposition of amplitudes; the lesson means the effective particle-level model is nonlinear.

assertions.value: The authors state that nonlinear optics studies how light interacts with materials to produce effects that depend on the light's intensity, making these effects nonlinear in relation to the strength of the underlying fields.
quotes: studies how light interacts with materials to produce effects that depend on the light's intensity, making these effects nonlinear in relation to the strength of the underlying fields
assertions.certainty_reason: The lesson opens with this definition.

assertions.value: The authors state that nonlinearity is the key to quantum optics because it is how interesting quantum states of light are produced.
quotes: it is the key to quantum optics because it is how we can produce interesting quantum states of light

assertions.value: The authors state that nonlinearity introduces necessary complexity within their reservoir systems.
quotes: It also introduces necessary complexity within our reservoir systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: A company describes its own reservoir product.
assertions.reader_inference: The lesson gives no mechanism or measurement here; it points to a separate lesson on reservoir computing.

assertions.value: The authors state that linear optics is the regime where the dynamics are well approximated as linear in the electromagnetic fields of the light, and that under a linear model increasing the light intensity only leads to brighter light.
quotes: Linear optics is a subfield of optics, which focuses on the regime where the dynamics are well approximated as being linear in electromagnetic fields of the light in the system.
increasing the light intensity will only lead to brighter light

assertions.value: The authors state that for strong enough fields linear optics always breaks down as an approximation, and that a consequence of quantum field theory is that this breakdown occurs even for light particles in vacuum.
quotes: For strong enough fields, linear optics always breaks down as an approximation.
a consequence of quantum field theory is that this breakdown even occurs for light particles in vacuum

assertions.value: The authors state that classically, linear optical systems are simple to describe mathematically, but that their behavior is not easy to solve mathematically when quantum states of light such as single light particles are considered.
quotes: linear optical systems are simple to describe mathematically
the behavior of such systems is not easy to solve mathematically when quantum states of light
assertions.reader_inference: The lesson names no complexity result for this; it is not a claim about boson sampling or any specific hardness theorem.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum states of light cannot be produced using linear optics, and that just weakening a light field, a linear process, cannot produce interesting quantum states of light.
quotes: Such states cannot be produced using linear optics
just weakening a light field (a linear process) cannot produce interesting quantum states of light

assertions.value: The authors describe the quantum Zeno blockade as an extreme example of nonlinear behavior, where even a single light particle can change the behavior of another light particle by effectively measuring it.
quotes: An extreme example of nonlinear behavior is the quantum Zeno blockade, where even a single light particle can change the behavior of another light particle by effectively "measuring" it.
assertions.certainty_reason: A company describes the effect its own technology uses.

assertions.value: The authors state that the process underlying the blockade is sum frequency generation, in which two light particles of different frequency combine to create a particle whose frequency is the sum of the two, and that this process is nonlinear in the fields of the light.
quotes: The underlying process that leads to the blockade is a process known as sum frequency generation
where two light particles of a different frequency combine to create another particle that has a frequency equal to the sum of the two
Such a process is clearly nonlinear in the fields of the light.

assertions.value: The authors write that nothing happens unless both frequencies are present, in which case no light at the combined frequency is produced.
quotes: Nothing happens unless both frequencies are present, in which case no light at the combined frequency is produced.
assertions.reader_inference: The sentence contradicts the sum frequency generation description before it. The intended meaning is almost certainly that light at the combined frequency is produced when both frequencies are present. Entered as printed; the coordinator should not store it as a physics claim without a correction note.

assertions.value: The authors state that the nonlinear process can be used for other tasks, for example producing a source of single light particles, and that the kind of process underlying this effect is parametric processes, which have their own lesson.
quotes: This nonlinear process can be used for many other tasks, for example, producing a source of single light particles
are parametric processes, they are important enough to be given their own lesson

assertions.value: The authors conclude that linear equations, in particular linear differential equations, can be solved using superposition, whereas nonlinear equations cannot be solved this way, so adding nonlinearity adds complexity.
quotes: Linear equations, in particular linear differential equations, can be solved by using the superposition property
nonlinear equations cannot be solved in this way
adding nonlinearity is a way of adding complexity

assertions.value: The authors conclude that quantum mechanics is technically a linear theory, but that this description is valid on a state space often impractically large for calculations, so it is often more practical to use nonlinear descriptions in terms of individual particles.
quotes: Quantum mechanics is technically a linear theory, but this description is only valid on a state space which is often impractically large to be used in calculations.
it is often more practical to work with more tractable nonlinear descriptions of these systems in terms of individual particles
